promise: Re-shoot a product video from one storyboard in landscape, vertical and square formats.
audience: People and agents producing repeatable videos of real web interfaces.
trigger: Validate, record, compose or re-shoot a storyboard-driven app teaser.

examples.title: Fictional app re-shoot
examples.brief: Inspect TeaserKit’s help and validate the included fictional demo storyboard. Explain the output shapes and the browser/ffmpeg prerequisites before proposing a build. Do not configure an AI provider, record a real product or generate a film during this first check.
examples.before: A manually recorded film requires a complete re-edit.
examples.after: The storyboard changes the one beat and preserves the edit in three shapes.
examples.why: The retained native capture/composition pipeline is independently useful to callers without Sizzle.

marketing.headline: Change the interface. Re-shoot the same story.
marketing.lead: For people producing repeatable product videos of web apps. TeaserKit writes the clicks, framing, captions and timing into a storyboard, then builds landscape, vertical and square outputs from that shared source.

benefits.title: Keep the edit repeatable
benefits.body: Update a beat after the UI changes instead of reconstructing the entire capture by hand.

benefits.title: Frame each shape deliberately
benefits.body: Give vertical and square their own regions of interest rather than relying on a crop of the landscape edit.

benefits.title: Review the whole output
benefits.body: Use validation, contact sheets, posters and build records to inspect timing, framing and accidental leaks.

walkthrough.title: Write and validate the storyboard
walkthrough.detail: Use the included fictional demo or scaffold your own project. Check beats, steps, captions and duration before recording.

walkthrough.title: Record and compose
walkthrough.detail: Drive the live web app with Playwright, then render captions, camera moves, aspect-specific framing and the soundtrack.

walkthrough.title: Inspect before sharing
walkthrough.detail: Read the contact sheets, watch the outputs and check for private text, spinners and broken layouts.

use_when: A product video must be re-shot as the interface evolves.
One story needs landscape, vertical and square versions.
An agent should call a repeatable library rather than improvise a manual film edit.
not_for: A model requirement for deterministic recording and rendering.
Calling a video finished before reviewing its frames and output.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Inspect TeaserKit’s help and validate the included fictional demo storyboard. Explain the output shapes and the browser/ffmpeg prerequisites before proposing a build. Do not configure an AI provider, record a real product or generate a film during this first check.
marketing.output_preview:
One storyboard
  beats: browser steps, hold, caption, duration
  framing: region of interest for each aspect

Build outputs
  landscape.mp4   vertical.mp4   square.mp4
  no-audio copies and posters
  contact sheets and build record

Review gate: inspect frames and watch the outputs before sharing.
marketing.example_note: Illustrative output layout for a fictional web app. No new film was produced for this marketing update.
install_notes: Python 3.11+, ffmpeg and Playwright Chromium are required for a full build.
The deterministic library/CLI works without an AI provider. Optional plan, explore and review use the separately configured ai extra.
Install the package first, inspect teaserkit doctor, then install any missing browser or renderer prerequisites deliberately.
The shown virtual-environment commands use macOS/Linux paths; on Windows, use the corresponding .venv\Scripts executables.
marketing.proof_summary: Deterministic and mocked checks plus installed storyboard validation passed. The full capture/render end-to-end check is separate; this update generated no new video.
marketing.next_step: Validate the included fictional storyboard, then review prerequisites before your first full build.

name: amplifier-capability-teaserkit
version_basis: Existing project metadata; not a new published tag or package release; an exact Git pin selects source for the shared portable installer.

native.status: Existing declared entrypoints preserved; runtime signatures, service access and installation tests remain separate evidence.

installation.scope: Shared canonical portable installer only; not the legacy repository helper or native package installation.

runtime.status: Host/caller authorizes each operation; installation is not a tool allowlist or standing approval.
declared_boundaries: Deterministic validation and rendering do not require a model key; optional plan/explore/review capabilities can incur provider cost.
Browser/ffmpeg prerequisites are explicit and are not installed as an unrequested side effect.
No new film, live browser recording or paid provider call was performed in this local packaging baseline.

secret_names.native_runtime_inventory: See native documentation; no credentials are bundled or inferred.

dataflow.installation: Shared canonical portable installer only (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/): read portable source tracked at the explicit Git pin and copy locally with SHA-256 receipts; no source text is transmitted. Legacy repository helpers copy current working-tree files and do not uniformly enforce Git pins, tracked membership or hash receipts. Native package builds and downloads have separate network, execution and storage flows described in their installation documentation.
dataflow.method: Caller supplies authorized context; existing promise and boundaries govern output.
dataflow.native_runtime: Provider/network/storage flows are owned by native interfaces and host authorization; these files do not enable them.

source_policy.revision: The shared canonical portable installer (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/) requires an explicit full 40-character Git commit and never infers latest. This guarantee does not apply uniformly to legacy or native installers; the legacy repository helper is an operator-controlled working-tree copy without Git-pin, tracked-membership or SHA-256 receipt enforcement.
source_policy.repository_rename: Public identity may change; skill folder, imports, entrypoints, tool IDs and schemas remain stable.
source_policy.research: .research/market remains local and ignored; AGENTS governs refresh.

film.heading: Change the interface. Re-shoot the same story.
film.blurb: In 71 seconds, a design change moves one button and Clix, the cursor in your product video, clicks where it used to be. TeaserKit writes the video down once as a storyboard, so you change one beat and rebuild landscape, vertical and square from the same story. Words on the deny list stop the recording if they appear, and you still watch every frame before you share. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: The app in it, Acme Planner, is a fictional demo. The film shows how the tool behaves; it does not report results.

shared_portable.applies_when: portable_method is declared; otherwise describe native interfaces without executing installation
guarantees: Tracked portable source membership and source-byte checks

legacy_repository.documentation: Existing install_commands and repository installation documentation, where provided.
legacy_repository.source_policy: Operator-controlled current working-tree copy. It can include untracked files and can operate outside a Git checkout; no uniform Git pin or SHA-256 transaction receipt is enforced.
legacy_repository.permissions: Review the specific command and destination; shared-installer transaction and permission guarantees do not describe this route.

native.documentation: interfaces.native, runtime_install_commands and project installation documentation, where provided.
native.source_policy: Native packaging, host composition and download routes retain their own version and provenance rules; shared portable receipt guarantees do not automatically apply.
native.permissions: Package builds may execute build tools; dependency or artifact downloads may use the network. Review the documented command, dependencies, destination and runtime authorization separately.
